links.reason: 1470 has the chief queen faint at the king's cut chest (கண்டேதன் கைசோர்ந்து ... வெற்றுடல மாயினாள்) and 293 has women beat breasts and wail (புலம்பினாரே); women mourning a fallen king is a stock scene, not a distinctive shared image. The teaches sentence only restates the shared theme of grief.

Both verses use the ghee-fed flame: 1018 நெய்சொரி கூரழல் போல்வதோர் புலவி, 988 நெய்பெய் நீளெரி ... கைசெய் மாலைபோற் கரிந்து. The roles differ (the sulk is the fire; the girl is the garland burnt by it), but the same uncommon figure set on the two women's passions for one man is meaningful.

2060 says heaven's wealth ends (ஒருநாள் ஈறுடைய) and 2068 has the sage set out இறுதியிலாப் பேரின்பம், so the verbal answer of end and endlessness is real. But both are steps of one sermon in its own order, which the plot already records, and 2060's மிசை is uncertain.
links.text_issue: 2068 line 1 உறுதிகணன் is a doubtful word.

links.reason: 204's soothsayer warns நீ ஒருவன் மேல் கொற்றம் வைப்பின் நிலம் திரு நீங்கும, naming no man, and 241 has the very holder of that power say a deity bids him செகுத்திடு the king. A prophecy and its fruit, and the teaches point that the warning is structural (ஒருவன்) is borne out by the Tamil.

962 has the practiser yoke the plough of zeal, till யாக்கைச் செறு and guard it with the five senses until வீட்டின்பம் grows, all his own labour; Tirumanthiram 1875 says the Lord ஆவி உழவுகொண்டானே, the Lord tills the soul. On this defensible reading the shared farm figure carries incompatible accounts of who works release, effort or grace.

49 states the soul is other than the body (உடம்பின் வேறாம் உயிர்) and proposes leaving the body in the Jinas' refuge; Kural 338 likens the body-life tie to a bird leaving its குடம்பை. The couplet does not call the tie 'light', and the epic only acts out a shared idea, so the couplet gains nothing beyond an illustration.

2780 scorns those who cut a lamb (கண்ணார் மறியறுத்து) saying the gods enjoy it, with recompense in நமனுலகு; Kural 259 sets not killing one creature above ஆயிரம் வேட்டல். Both refuse blood sacrifice, so the relation is agreement in two modes, not a limit or condition one puts on the other.
links.text_issue: 2780 நான்மடங்கு is uncertain (fourfold or a fourth).

links.reason: 427 recommends Marusi as one who can say சுற்றமும் கருமமும், and 578 only has him promise to tell the descent, the entry and the king's words. A promise to report is not a test of the ministers' reason; the link is story sequence with a generic trait.

1483 has the king taken down from the elephant's brow (மதயானை ... நுதலினிழித்து) and given to the fire on a bed of பஞ்சுந் துகிலும், and Naladiyar 21 says umbrella kings on elephants (யானைத் தலைமிசை) died. The connection is real but the other side gains no named king (the verse names none), and teaches is only the stock lesson that rank does not save.

Yasodhara 240 lists அறிவு காட்சி ஒழுக்கம் and their fruits (heaven, rule, release) and Neelakesi 116 calls the triple discipline a மருந்து for birth. The two state the same doctrine; the medical frame adds a figure but no limit or condition, so qualifies does not fit.

1572 and 1573 are one speech of the jester in consecutive verses: the boast (வாதம் வல்லன) and the method (தடியாலே மோதி வெல்வன்). The later verse is the continuation of a sentence, not an answer or reversal, and the reading of line 3 is uncertain.
links.text_issue: 1573 line 3 தடியாலே reading is not certain.

links.reason: Both define faith (காட்சி) as clarity: Yasodhara 241 அகத்தெழு தெளிவு, Neelakesi 121 ... வேட்கையது வாந்தெளிவு, the latter adding eight things கடவுள் முதலாய to hold in mind. Neelakesi gives no list of acts and freedoms, and its eight are objects, not 'the one with eight excellent things', so the contrast is overstated.

78 lists சங்கு and திகிரி on the younger prince's palm; 109 has the court affirm, after a speech (என்றவன் இயம்ப), that Tivittan will rule ஒருகுடை நீழல். 109 does not mention the body marks, so making it a reading of 78's portrait depends on an inference the Tamil does not state.

814 says a lion (செறியெயிற் றாளி) routs an elephant herd and one tiger a deer herd; Kural 500 says a jackal kills the elephant காலாழ் களரில். These are different situations, the strong one's nature and the weak one's ground, and both can hold, so there is no incompatible claim; the gains invent a rival explanation.

1577 builds the ஊன்பயில் குரம்பை of bone, sinew, flesh and nine doors and 1578 names its builder வினைப்பெருந் தச்சன்; Thiruppugazh 894 calls the same nine-gated body நான்முக னெடுத்த வீடு. On that reading the inventory is shared and the maker is a god in one and the deed in the other, a real doctrinal disagreement.
links.text_issue: Depends on 1578 for the builder; 1577 line 4 can divide as நல்லன் or அல்லன்.

links.reason: 427 praises Marusi as one who can say the fit thing (உற்றன உய்த்துரைக்கும் ஆற்றலான்), and in 529 he confesses பொருந்தாக் கறையவா மொழிகள் சொன்னேன் and is ashamed before the king's forbearance. The irony qualifies the ministers' praise, and 531 does show him turning to a new argument.
links.text_issue: 529 lines 1-2 are compressed; 427 line 2 is uncertain.

links.reason: 1240 calls the god காதிகண் ணரிந்த, the one who cut away his own ghati karmas; Tirumanthiram 1527 has grace come குருவென வந்து and the soul's agency end (தன்செய லற்றால்). The epic verse says nothing about how the worshipper is released, so the incompatibility is drawn from general doctrine and not from what the two verses claim.

Yasodhara 233 gives the freed soul எண்குணங்கள் with அனந்தமா மறிவு காட்சி; Tirumanthiram 444 says of Siva குணம் எண்குண மாகும். The list is shared and the owner differs, which teaches states, but 444 does not deny that freed souls have such qualities, so these are not incompatible claims.
links.text_issue: 233 line 2 திருமல நித்தமாகி is not sure.

links.reason: 1931's tormentors are only தூர்த்தத் தொழிலவர் who say முன்னதிற் செய்த வினையின் ... எய்துமின்; Tirumanthiram 198's வல்லடிக் காரர் bind those who said கொல்லிடு குத்து. Neither verse names Death as master, and 1931's silence about whom they serve is no counter-claim, so the 'tension' is built on an absence.

27 in the patikam says Civakan அறம் கேட்டு ... அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த, and 2811 gives part of the sermon: யாக்கைகொண் டவர்கட்கு யாவதுந் துன்பம். The fulfilment is real, but a prologue summary will match any later scene it summarises, and 27 names fear of kingship rather than embodiment as the motive.

Both orders are to recover the herd at speed (432 காற்றின் விரைந்து தொறுமீட்கென, 1858 வல்லே படுநிரை பெயர்க்க), so the repeated scene is real. The contrast between real hunters and friends' staged raid comes from the plot, not these verses, and 'his rage meets no enemy' goes beyond them.

1494 likens the lovers to those with சாதலும் பிறப்பும் இல்லாத் தன்மை; Kural 1103 asks whether தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு is sweeter than the beloved's arms. The pairing of erotic bliss with the highest state is real, but the epic does not 'answer' the couplet, and 'two months' is not in either text.

Kar Narpathu 9 has the flowers speak இன்சொற் பலவும் announcing his return; Akananuru 74 has the heroine say she could hold to the friend's வன்புறை இன்சொல் நன்பல were it not for the evening குழல். The second limits the comfort the first offers, at a named hour, which is what qualifies means.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 9 line 1 உருவினை is unclear.

links.reason: 1453 is the fire weapon and 1454 the வாருணம் arrow that puts it out, consecutive moves in one duel. A weapon and its counter in the next verse are plot sequence, and 'matched counters' is a generic remark.

1459 has the king's திகிரி hide the hero in flame and 1461 has the hero salute the discus and send it back to split the king's chest (மன்னனை மார்பு கீண்டு). That is a reversal, the weapon passing to the enemy, but there are no incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type.

Udayana 181 has பேய்க்கணம் dance and நரி feed on the slain amid the kings' ascent, without pity; Siddhar 354 lists fire, worm, earth, kite, jackal and dog claiming the body. The jackal on corpses is a common figure, and reading the battle as the Siddhar's lesson imposes a meaning the epic verse does not carry.

Udayana 365 burns இருவினை by தியானம், and Tirumanthiram 219 has deeds fall when அங்கி is worshipped and rises (அங்கி வினைசுடும்). 219 names a ritual fire, not the Lord's, so the teaches and gains that cast it as divine grace against self-effort misstate the Saiva side; the real contrast is ritual against meditation.
links.text_issue: Udayana 365 has five lines; 219 line 4 வீழிசெய்து is obscure.

links.reason: Akananuru 168's Udhiyan is the கொடைக்கடன் ஏன்ற lord of குழுமூர் whose அட்டில் roars; Puram 2 praises பெருஞ்சோற்று Udhiyan Cheralathan who gave பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம். The Tamil does not fix that these are one king, and Puram 2 does not say to whom the food went, so the note overstates it.

Soolamani 200 calls the feet of the one யாதியந் தகன்று நின்ற the refuge that ends great suffering, and Tirumanthiram 138 calls the feet Sivam, Sivaloka, the path and தஞ்சம். Both make the feet a refuge, but 200 does not deny they are the goal; the contrast rests on silence and on 202, which describes the state of those who keep the teaching.

720 gives the lute's wood a mother (இருநில மடந்தை) and a foster mother (கைத்தாய்) in the sky, and 328 has Kandukkatan hand the child to his wife. 328 uses no shared word or figure, so seeing Civakan's birth in the lute's pedigree is a symbolic reading the Tamil does not set up.

Tirumanthiram 144 says only கொண்ட விரதமும் ஞானமும் go with the dead, and Naga Kumara 152 has the fast and gifts bring இந்திர பதம், kingship and then பஞ்சம கதி. The epic extends the rule rather than limiting it, and the Saiva verse gains nothing from a Jain ladder of rewards it would not accept.

514 is the Vidyadhara king's ஓலை to the lord of Podanam sending gifts; 662 is a letter read and repeated (ஓலை கொடொப்ப) before the king, its demand coming only in 663-665. The gift and demand contrast is real in the plot, but 662 itself carries none of it and is corrupt.
links.text_issue: 662's last word உரைத்தர் is short a syllable and line 3 is clipped; 514 line 4 is doubtful.

links.reason: Yasodhara 22 orders the twin children (மக்களிரட்டையர்) brought, after the people have urged the king to appease the goddess lest she bring disease (15-16); Kural 327 says தன்னுயிர் நீப்பினும் do not take another's இன்னுயிர். The scene puts the rule to a case it does not foresee, killing to protect one's people.

1101 sets the priest's offering beside the groom's desire with one verb, அழல் ... வேட்டான் / மடந்தையை ... வேட்டான், and Siddhar 147 kindles ஓமக் கனல் within to cross காமக் கடல். The homa fire is shared, but in 1101 the fire does not kindle the desire, so 'one fire serves desire' overstates the epic side.

947 has Civakan give the dying dog the five (ஐந்து நினைத்திடு) so it is freed of நீனிற வினை, and 1156 has the god who was that dog sense his benefactor's peril and descend. A deed and its fruit across the story, which is the kind of within-epic link the brief allows.

109 says kings linger in desire (ஆசைப் பட்டு அரசு வைக) in the courtesans' courtyards, and 206 warns that many who sank in போகமே got பாவமும் பழியும். The theme is shared, but 109 is a city catalogue about kings in general, and 'quietly prepares the charge' is an interpretation the verse does not signal.

Kural 872's வில்லேர் உழவர் and Thinaimozhi 17's வில்லுழுது வாழ்நர் share a distinctive figure, the bow as plough. But the venba sets no contrast with word-ploughmen: her slack shoulders come from his leaving நல்காது for wealth, not from any word or promise, so teaches reads the couplet into it.

Soolamani 620's king மாற்றம் பொறான் is the opposite of Kural 389's சொற்பொறுக்கும் வேந்தன். The verse only illustrates the couplet's virtue by its lack, with no test or limit, and the couplet gains nothing but an example.

2439's dresser prints the திலகம் with her curved nail for Ilakkanai and 350's Vijayai removes the திலகம் with her finger along with குண்டலம் and pearls. Putting the mark on and taking it off is a meaningful pairing, but it is not two incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type.

Soolamani 395's ஆழிக் காதி is the Jina's dharma-wheel emblem, while Tirumanthiram 349's ஆழி கொடுத்தனன் அச்சுதற்கு is Vishnu's discus, and 349's first ஆழி may be the sea. The shared word names two different things, so there is no claim about one wheel's source to disagree over.

Naladiyar 200 says கருனைச்சோறு ஆர்வர் கயவர், while for the self-reliant தாளாண்மை நீரும் அமிழ்தாய் விடும்; Nanmanikkadigai 66 says அரிசியான் இன்புறூஉங் கீழ் and the high take delight in வரிசை. Both mark the base by rice, and the different opposites, effort and due rank, are a real and specific contrast.

1472's உண்ணிறை நாணும் உடைந்தன takes up Kural 1251's நிறையென்னும் நாணுத்தாழ் ... உடைக்கும், the same pair of words and verb. The couplet speaks in separation and the epic sets the breaking at first sight (கண்ணுறக் காளையைக் காண்டலும்), which is a real development, though the 'omen' point comes from the plot.

527 has the king say only முன்னவன் செய்த ... வினைகளே முயல்வது, and Kural 377 says one enjoys only as வகுத்தான் வகுத்த வகை. The pairing is apt, but the epic-side gain is untrue: the king does state a general rule (இன்னவன் இன்ன நீரான் இன்னவே எய்துக).

990 says if she forgot him விதிநனி துரப்ப மீட்டு நினைப்பதே, and Kural 1125 says உள்ளுவன் மன்யான் மறப்பின் மறப்பறியேன். Both deny forgetting by turning on the logic of remembering, and only the epic names a cause (விதி), so the pairing teaches something specific.
